TCP client 收發。本組全部走 buffer 模式（QIOPEN 末參數: TCP client send and receive. Everything in this group runs in buffer mode (last QIOPEN parameter 0) — ⚠ incoming data does NOT show up in the terminal by itself: the module emits a single +QIURC: "recv",<id> notification, and you have to press Read Data (AT+QIRD) yourself to fetch it, repeating the read until it returns +QIRD: 0 — otherwise the module will never issue the next notification. If no notification arrives, first check whether AT+QURCCFG="urcport" on the Hardware page is set to uart1 — if it is not, every URC is going out of the USB port instead. Also, the default peer tcpbin.com has two quirks found by measurement (2026-08-07): ① it is a "line-oriented" echo server, so unless the data you send ends with a newline (hex 0A) it just keeps buffering and sends nothing back (without 0A, 6 s passed with no response; after appending a single 0A it came back within 0.1 s); ② it has a 15 s idle timeout — send nothing for 15 s and it closes the connection on its own, and you get +QIURC: "closed",0. That is not a bad thing: it is a ready-made way to test "the peer drops the connection" without running a server of your own. After the closed notification the socket sits in the closing state, and ⚠ you must run AT+QICLOSE=0 before connectID 0 can be reused, otherwise QIOPEN returns error 563.
要連線的伺服器 IP 位址或域名。預設 tcpbin.com 是免費公開的 TC: The server IP address or domain name to connect to. The default tcpbin.com is a free public TCP echo service: it returns whatever you send, with no registration, no server of your own and no router configuration — the module is a TCP client dialing outward, which is the only direction that always works in a consumer environment. ⚠ But it has a "15 s idle timeout" (measured 2026-08-07: the FIN arrived 15.1 s after a line was sent; also 15.1 s when nothing at all was sent after connecting): go past it and it closes the connection on its own and the module emits +QIURC: "closed",0 — that is not something your AT+QIRD press caused. To hold the connection open, send data at least once every 10 s (for example AT+QISENDEX=0,"0A"); TCP keepalive will not stop it, and the Keepalive group description explains why.
TCP 層的保活探測（手冊 §2.3.1 AT+QICFG=\"tcp/keep: TCP-layer keepalive probing (manual §2.3.1 AT+QICFG="tcp/keepalive"). ⚠ Against tcpbin.com's 15 s idle timeout it is "completely useless" — measured with keepalive on, the connection was still closed at 15.1 s: keepalive sends empty probe packets at the TCP layer, which the application never sees, while tcpbin counts "has any application data arrived"; and interval_time has a minimum of 25 s anyway, already longer than 15 s. The only way to survive an application-layer timeout is to send real data (for example a newline every 10 s with AT+QISENDEX=0,"0A"). Where it genuinely helps is "keeping the carrier's NAT mapping alive and detecting dead connections" — the NAT mapping of an IoT SIM is reclaimed after a few idle minutes, which is a disconnection at another level. The parameter ranges come from the manual; press QICFG=? to see the ranges this firmware actually reports (no traffic).
